title: $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is thick and essentially small
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, and use the fixed-universe small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring: a finite discrete commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$, with the coefficient objects of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and write $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of its module objects. Write $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Then $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is a thick triangulated subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ [pur9-def-thick], and it is essentially small, meaning that its objects have a set of representatives up to isomorphism in that fixed universe.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal M=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. Sheaf tensor and internal modules make $\mathcal M$ Grothendieck. Its maps are small sets of sectionwise natural linear families. K-injectives and derived local smallness give small ambient Hom sets in the fixed universe.

For finite $A$, the exact coefficient equivalence identifies finite constant local models on every scheme $T$, and its forward functor keeps the underlying abelian sheaf. Internal restriction to a stratum has the inverse image as underlying sheaf, as ordinary restriction does, and the canonical coefficient identifications commute with that restriction; hence the equivalence matches the two constructible hearts on the same stratifications. Finite $A$-modules are finitely presented, since finite free surjections have finite kernels. Ordinary constructible Serre closure therefore gives internal heart closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions.

source.place: Finite discrete encoding and heart closure (original steps 2, 8)

proof.text: Use rational-heart closure for $E,\Qlb$ and integral constant-model closure for $\mathcal O_E$, read in internal modules through the sectionwise equivalence, which keeps underlying sheaves, kernels and cokernels. The case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes $\mathbf Q_\ell,\mathbf Z_\ell$. Rank-zero models give zero; composing local isomorphisms gives repleteness. Every admissible heart is thus a weak Serre class.

Apply the weak-Serre bounded-thickness lemma to this heart. It gives thick $\Dbc$, including all ambient retracts. Finite Tor amplitude is thick by its well-definedness theorem, so the intersection $\Dctf$ is thick.

On each stratum finite scalar matrices give a small family of cokernel models. Localization and cartesian coefficients identify covering-object restrictions with slice-site models, and the sectionwise equivalence reads internal modules as module sheaves. Prescribed-local-model smallness gives a small representing family on that stratum.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: local models and overlap data (original step 5)

proof.text: Locally Noetherian $X$ is quasi-separated, hence qcqs, so constructibility uses one global finite stratification. Fix a finite stratification and stratum representatives $B_s$. Exact stratum pullbacks jointly detect zero; the adjoint-model lemma embeds every realizing $F$ into $P=\prod_s a_{s*}B_s$. Subobjects of $P$ form a set: their image subsheaves are families of subsets of $P(V)$ on the small site. Finite stratifications and tuples form a set in the fixed bound. Their union represents the constructible heart.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: stratifications, embeddings, subobjects (original steps 3-7)

proof.text: For fixed $[a,b]$, use ambient truncations $T_q=\tau_{\le q}K$: $T_{a-1}\simeq0$, $T_b\simeq K$, and $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(K)[-q]\to T_{q-1}[1]$. The small-extension lemma inductively counts the $T_q$ from the heart representatives and the previous family. Union over integer intervals gives a small family for $\Dbc$. Retain its finite-Tor representatives; isomorphism invariance covers every $\Dctf$ object.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: ambient Postnikov triangles and extension counting (original steps 11-13)

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs, with four statement-only subarguments extracted; old arguments and exact allocation retained in report.md.

lean.note: Maintainer second-reader fix (NT-cc-Q02 review of 815504937e63): the size conclusion was written `ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall (…)` with no universe, so Lean generalized it to a fresh universe parameter: the theorem was det_brown_hypotheses_small.{u, u_1} and claimed essential smallness in every universe u_1, including u_1 < u, which is false (e.g. Spec of a field in Type 1 with more quadratic extensions than any Type-0 cardinal has too many rank-one constructible F_3-sheaves).
